title: The Shapes of Cells
description: Necrosis melts cells into shapeless blobs. Learn how a cell's shape fits its job to restore piece 4.

content.value: Cells are not all the same shape. Their shape usually matches the JOB they do. Most cells are round, oval, or box-like, but some have very special shapes suited to their work.

CELL              SHAPE           WHY
🧠  Nerve cell     long & branched  to carry signals far
🩸  Red blood cell round disc       to flow easily & carry oxygen
💪  Muscle cell    long & spindle   to contract and relax
🧅  Onion cell     neat brick-like  to build plant tissue

A nerve cell is long and thread-like so it can carry messages across long distances in the body. A red blood cell is a flexible round disc so it can squeeze through tiny blood vessels while carrying oxygen. The shape is designed for the task.

The outer CELL MEMBRANE gives a cell its shape and holds it together. In plant cells an extra tough CELL WALL outside the membrane gives them a fixed, boxy shape — which is why plant cells look so neat and regular.
A great rule in biology: 'form fits function'. If you know a cell's shape, you can often guess its job — and vice versa.
Key Takeaway: Cells have different shapes suited to their functions — nerve cells are long, red blood cells are round discs. The cell membrane (and cell wall in plants) gives a cell its shape.
